content:
The [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Format and validate YAML — clean indentation, clear error messages. Enter your YAML and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Format and validate YAML in one place: paste YAML and get it back with clean two-space indentation, or a clear error message pointing at the problem when it does not parse. YAML's indentation is its structure, so a single misplaced space breaks a file — this tool catches that before the file reaches your app. Everything runs in your browser; your content is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the YAML Formatter/Validator

Start by typing or pasting your YAML. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your YAML into the editor (or use the sample).
2. Click Format & Validate — formatted YAML appears, or an error message explains the problem.
3. Copy the formatted result.

## How it works

The [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Formatting `site: {name: My Site}` expands the flow style into indented lines. A tab-indented line returns an error naming the line, because YAML does not allow tabs for indentation. Try the same figures in the [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Common YAML mistakes it catches

Tabs used for indentation (YAML requires spaces), inconsistent indentation, unquoted values containing a colon, and duplicate keys. The error message names the line and the reason, which is usually enough to fix the file.

## Where YAML shows up

Configuration files, CI pipelines, Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests, and front matter in Markdown files. Any of them breaks on a small indentation error, which is why validating before saving is worth the seconds it takes.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use spaces, never tabs — YAML forbids tabs for indentation.
- Quote values that contain a colon or start with a special character.
- Validate a config file here before pasting it into your project.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a YAML validator do?

It parses your YAML and reports errors — bad indentation, tabs, duplicate keys — with the line number, so you can fix the file before it breaks your app. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does YAML care about indentation?

In YAML, indentation is the structure: it shows which values belong to which key. A line indented one space too far belongs to a different key, or to no key at all. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my YAML uploaded anywhere?

No. Parsing and formatting run entirely in your browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML Formatter/Validator](/yaml-formatter-validator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the YAML Formatter/Validator?

Just YAML. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
